card: Adds the `p2p_transport_v2_receive` fuzz target to exercise BIP 324 `V2Transport` byte reception. Existing fuzz tests do not feed malformed or arbitrary byte streams past the initial key exchange, leaving transport error handling and receive state transitions under-tested. The author notes the target crafts streams containing arbitrary bytes mixed with corrupted handshake segments in variable slice sizes, reaching all receive states without crashes under ASan and UBSan.
changed_since_previous: Now includes the complete patch implementing the `p2p_transport_v2_receive` fuzz target.
evidence: PR description: 'No fuzz target feeds V2Transport bytes that an honest peer would not send past the v2 key exchange.'
Author reports running the target for 13 minutes under libFuzzer with ASan/UBSan without crashes, confirming it successfully exercises both accepted and rejected message handling paths.
problem: Existing fuzz targets do not feed malformed or arbitrary byte streams to `V2Transport` past the initial key exchange, leaving post-handshake BIP 324 receive state transitions and error handling under-tested against hostile peer traffic.

risk.why: Only adds a new fuzzing target; no production or consensus code is touched.

scope_notes: Adds a single standalone fuzz target in `src/test/fuzz/p2p_transport_serialization.cpp`.
summary: Adds the `p2p_transport_v2_receive` fuzz target to test BIP 324 `V2Transport` message reception. The target generates byte streams containing mixtures of arbitrary data and valid or bit-flipped handshake elements (keys, garbage, terminators, encrypted packets) and feeds them in arbitrary slice sizes to reach all receive states and failure transitions.
